claims.explanation: The selective killing pattern is most strongly associated with loss of PTEN and activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, as PTEN-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines and PTEN wild-type lines among resistant lines. This may reflect a synthetic lethal interaction between PI3K/AKT activation and the angiotensin AT2 receptor (AGTR2) signaling, which can promote apoptosis via nitric oxide and cGMP; PD-123319 blocks AGTR2, potentially exacerbating survival signaling in PTEN-deficient cells. Other features such as KRAS mutation and EGFR mutation may contribute but are less consistent.

features.basis: Enriched in sensitive lines (UACC62, FTC133, KALS1) and absent in many resistant lines; PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, which may interact with AGTR2 blockade.
PD-123319 is an AGTR2 antagonist; AGTR2 signaling can promote apoptosis via nitric oxide/cGMP, so low AGTR2 expression may reduce drug effect.
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines (OV7, CL11, KPNSI9S) but also in resistant lines, suggesting a context-dependent role.
EGFR-mutant lung lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006) are sensitive, while EGFR-mutant KYSE270 is resistant, indicating possible lineage-specific effects.
BRAF mutations are common in resistant melanoma lines (IGR37, LOXIMVI) but also in sensitive UACC62 and K029AX, so the effect is not consistent.
TP53 mutations are widespread across both sensitive and resistant lines, providing little discriminatory power.
PIK3CA mutations appear in several resistant lines (HGC27, SNUC5, MKN1) but also in sensitive KYSE510 and SNU840, suggesting a complex role.
NF1 mutations are present in sensitive lines (FTC133, BICR6, KALS1) but also in resistant lines (LOXIMVI, S117), so the effect is uncertain.
ARID1A mutations are found in resistant lines (SNUC5, HEC265, LOXIMVI) but also in sensitive KU1919, limiting confidence.
KMT2D mutations appear in resistant lines (SNUC5, HEC265, KE39, KYSE270) but also in sensitive KU1919 and BICR6, so the association is weak.
